","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

How to use ' Near Me':

  • Look Up an Address: Begin by entering the address you are interested in into the search bar.
  • Once the address is displayed, press the “Near Me” button.
  • The system will Show results from following layers for CBC & SRBC
  • LLPG Address
  • Community Centres and Village Halls
  • Post code zone
  • Wards
  • Parish
  • Polling District
  • Planning Application


The system will display number of features around the specified address.

Planning Application will be sorted by the latest date, with the most recent applications appearing first.

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Draw a point, Draw a polyline, Draw a polygon, Draw a rectangle, and Draw a circle—Sketch a feature on the map or scene.

  • Preview—View a preview of the symbology of the feature to be drawn.
  • Source—For points, select from a list of categories containing premade symbols. Different symbols are available in each category.
  • Symbol customization options—Select a predefined symbol from the box. Customize the symbol using the following settings:
  • Points—Customize size, fill color, outline color, outline width, and fill transparency. Only the size setting is available for picture point symbols.
  • Polylines—Customize width, dash type, color, and transparency.
  • Polygons, rectangles, and circles—Customize fill color, outline color, outline width, and transparency.
"},"id":"widget_2034"},"widget_2035":{"uri":"widgets/layout/row/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Block 447","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"number":[40,10,40,10],"unit":"px"}}},"id":"widget_2035","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1274"}}},"widget_2036":{"uri":"widgets/common/image/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Image 263","config":{"functionConfig":{"altText":"","toolTip":"","linkParam":{},"scale":"Fit","imageParam":{"url":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2036/1720019829594.png","originalUrl":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2036/1720019829594.png","fileName":"1720019829594.png","originalName":"chrome_5snsb1gU4z.png","imgSourceType":"BY_UPLOAD","fileFormat":"image/png","originalId":"1720019829594","isUseCompress":false,"originalWidth":589,"originalHeight":566},"imgSourceType":"","srcExpression":null,"imageFillMode":"FIT"},"styleConfig":{}},"id":"widget_2036","style":{"borderRadius":null,"border":{"color":"var(--light-300)","type":"solid","width":"2px"}}},"widget_2037":{"uri":"widgets/layout/column/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Column 568","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"space":[10],"unit":"px"},"justifyContent":"flex-start","alignItems":"stretch"}},"id":"widget_2037","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1275"}}},"widget_2038":{"uri":"widgets/common/text/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Text 500","config":{"placeholder":"

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"
  • Measurement tools—Include relevant measurements in appropriate units on drawn features.
  • For points, turn on Show location measurement to include degree minute second (DMS) or decimal degree (DD) measurements.
  • For polylines, turn on Show length measurement to include kilometer, meter, mile, or feet measurements.
  • For polygons, rectangles, and circles, turn on Show area measurement to include square kilometer, square meter, hectare, acre, square mile, or square feet measurements. Turn on Show perimeter measurement to include kilometer, meter, mile, or feet measurements.
"},"id":"widget_2038"},"widget_2039":{"uri":"widgets/layout/row/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Block 448","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"number":[40,10,40,10],"unit":"px"}}},"id":"widget_2039","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1276"}}},"widget_2040":{"uri":"widgets/common/image/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Image 264","config":{"functionConfig":{"altText":"","toolTip":"","linkParam":{},"scale":"Fit","imageParam":{"url":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2040/1720019942347.png","originalUrl":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2040/1720019942347.png","fileName":"1720019942347.png","originalName":"chrome_0lBgGDMwcf.png","imgSourceType":"BY_UPLOAD","fileFormat":"image/png","originalId":"1720019942347","isUseCompress":false,"originalWidth":901,"originalHeight":534},"imgSourceType":"","srcExpression":null,"imageFillMode":"FIT"},"styleConfig":{}},"id":"widget_2040","style":{"borderRadius":null,"border":{"color":"var(--light-300)","type":"solid","width":"2px"}}},"widget_2041":{"uri":"widgets/layout/column/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Column 569","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"space":[10],"unit":"px"},"justifyContent":"flex-start","alignItems":"stretch"}},"id":"widget_2041","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1277"}}},"widget_2042":{"uri":"widgets/common/text/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Text 501","config":{"placeholder":"

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"
  • Undo and Redo—Undo or redo actions. These buttons are based on the actions performed using the widget.
  • Clear all—Remove all drawn features from the currently active web map.
  • Expand and Collapse—When using the widget in toolbar mode, expand or collapse panels associated with the widget, including the customization panels for points, polylines, and other features.

Optionally, users can do any of the following: Click the Unit drop-down menu and select a different unit of measure. Measurement results convert to the newly selected unit. Click New measurement to start another measurement. Click Clear measurement  to clear the current measurement. The Measurement widget uses snapping—the pointer snaps to features on the map. You can press and hold the Ctrl key to temporarily turn off snapping. ﻿

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Search-To search, users type a word or phrase in the search box and press Enter, click the search button, or choose from a list of suggestions that appear based on matching records. (The suggestions list displays each matching value as an item, so if a record has two fields that match the search phrase, that record appears as two suggestions.) Users can use the Up and Down arrow keys to browse through the suggestions list. Clicking a suggestion replaces the search phrase with the content from the suggested item to apply the search using the new value, which returns corresponding data in a result panel.

following locators can be used to search:

  1. CBC and SRBC LLPG
  2. Royalmail Postcode Zone
  3. Points of interest
  4. Addresses
  5. UPRN of the Property
  6. UTM coordinates
  7. What3words
  8. deed reference number
  9. Land title
  10. UK Geocode to search using the lat long

Coordinates in a coordinate system that you specify with a well-known ID (WKID). The format for this is x, y: WKID. An example is -13046165.52, 4036389.847: 102100

Use current location—Include a suggestion option to search based on the user’s current location.

Recent searches—Display the search history in the suggestion box based on a specified maximum number of recent searches. (Users can clear the search history.)

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

The Select widget allows user to select features using attribute selection and interactive map selection. It also allow user to perform data processing tasks with a selection.

"},"id":"widget_2237"},"widget_2238":{"uri":"widgets/layout/row/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Block 497","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"number":[40,10,40,10],"unit":"px"}}},"id":"widget_2238","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1395"}}},"widget_2239":{"uri":"widgets/common/image/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Image 298","config":{"functionConfig":{"altText":"","toolTip":"","linkParam":{},"scale":"Fit","imageParam":{"url":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2239/1720429531490.png","originalUrl":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2239/1720429531490.png","fileName":"1720429531490.png","originalName":"chrome_uCnf7aFwP9.png","imgSourceType":"BY_UPLOAD","fileFormat":"image/png","originalId":"1720429531490","isUseCompress":false,"originalWidth":480,"originalHeight":549},"imgSourceType":"","srcExpression":null,"imageFillMode":"FIT"},"styleConfig":{}},"id":"widget_2239","style":{"borderRadius":null,"border":{"color":"var(--light-300)","type":"solid","width":"2px"}}},"widget_2240":{"uri":"widgets/layout/column/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Column 620","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"space":[10],"unit":"px"},"justifyContent":"flex-start","alignItems":"stretch"}},"id":"widget_2240","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1396"}}},"widget_2241":{"uri":"widgets/common/text/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Text 551","config":{"placeholder":"

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

There are two ways to select features:

  • Interactive selection—Interactive selection involves drawing a point, line, or shape on the map to select a set of features.

With interactive selection, users can select multiple features in the following four ways:

  1. New selection (click and drag the pointer to draw a shape)
  2. Add to the current selection (press Shift while drawing)
  3. Remove from the current selection (press Ctrl while drawing for Windows
  4. Select subset from the current selection (press Ctrl+Shift while drawing for Windows
  • Attribute selection—Attribute selection involves using SQL expressions to select features matching a selection criteria.


Interactive selection—These settings appear when you choose Interact with a Map

Tools—Choose which interactive map selection tools to include in the widget. You must turn on at least one tool.

Select by rectangle—Users can click and drag to draw a rectangle across features.

Select by lasso—Users can click the map to create the vertices of a polygon, or draw with the pointer to create a freehand shape. Users can double-click to close the polygon and select contained features.

Select by circle—Users can click and drag to draw a circle across a feature.

Select by line—Users can click the map to create the vertices of a line. Users can double-click to end the line and select intersecting features.

Select by point—Users can click the map to place a point and select intersecting features.

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

The Print widget provides users with the following tools:


Template—Select a print template.

Show print area—Add a rectangle to the map showing the print extent.

Print—Create a print result.

Print result—View print results. Click a result to open it in a new window.


User can also change these fields


Title—Specify the printed file name, and the map title when applicable.

Map printing extents—Choose how to calculate the map's printed extent.

  • Current map extent—Use the Map widget's current view.
  • Current map scale—Use the Map widget's current scale.
  • Set map scale—Provide an exact scale.

Output spatial reference—Define the output spatial reference of the print by specifying a valid well-known ID (WKID).

Print quality—Set the print resolution.

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

The Table widget displays interactive attribute tables for feature layers and scene layers with an associated feature layer with the option to include multiple sheets that users access from tabs or a list. You can choose which fields to include in the table and turn on tools such as search and selection. Users can sort tables by one or multiple fields and by ascending or descending order.

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Set Filter-A filter uses logical expressions to find and display features in a layer based on attribute values in its data. Expressions use the general form of <Field name> <operator that specifies a condition> <Value or Field>. For example, Shelter capacity is greater than 200.


To create expressions in the SQL Expression Builder, click Add clause or Add clause set.


The expression for each clause includes the following parts:


  • Field—Select a field from the data source to filter on. The three field types are number, string, and date. Representative icons appear next to the field names.
  • Operator—Select a functional operator to evaluate the data values for the selected field. Operators vary depending on the field type. View a full list of supported operators for each field type.
  • Value—Type or select a value to complete the clause. Click the Select source type button Select source type to choose a value, such as user input, field, unique, unique (predefined), multiple, and multiple (predefined).

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Add bookmark—Create one or more bookmarks. You can drag individual bookmarks to reorder them.


Set bookmark view—Zoom in to or search for a location using the map in the window that appears when you add a bookmark. You can define the extent and layer visibility and add drawing marks. You can resize and move the window, if needed. To reopen this window, click the Change the bookmark view button for each bookmark.

Bookmark title—Type a name for the bookmark. Click the Delete button to remove a bookmark.

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

The Coordinate Conversion widget allows you to input coordinates using one coordinate system and output to different coordinate systems using multiple notation formats. Another capability of this widget is to geocode and reverse geocode a captured point on the map.

"},"id":"widget_2465"},"widget_2466":{"uri":"widgets/layout/row/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Block 553","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"number":[40,10,40,10],"unit":"px"}}},"id":"widget_2466","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1535"}}},"widget_2467":{"uri":"widgets/common/image/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Image 334","config":{"functionConfig":{"altText":"","toolTip":"","linkParam":{},"scale":"Fit","imageParam":{"url":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2467/1720434998542.png","originalUrl":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2467/1720434998542.png","fileName":"1720434998542.png","originalName":"chrome_bdnP7zKSn7.png","imgSourceType":"BY_UPLOAD","fileFormat":"image/png","originalId":"1720434998542","isUseCompress":false,"originalWidth":477,"originalHeight":699},"imgSourceType":"","srcExpression":null,"imageFillMode":"FIT"},"styleConfig":{}},"id":"widget_2467","style":{"borderRadius":null,"border":{"color":"var(--light-300)","type":"solid","width":"2px"}}},"widget_2468":{"uri":"widgets/layout/column/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Column 680","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"space":[10],"unit":"px"},"justifyContent":"flex-start","alignItems":"stretch"}},"id":"widget_2468","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1536"}}},"widget_2469":{"uri":"widgets/common/text/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Text 607","config":{"placeholder":"

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

It provides users with the following tools and options:

Add Point—Click the map to capture coordinates on a connected map.

Copy All—Copy all output notation to the operating system's clipboard so it can be pasted into an external application such as Notepad.

Zoom—Zoom to the manually supplied or captured coordinates on the map in the input location.

Input Format Settings—Reconfigure the input notation and apply a custom format for how captured coordinates will be displayed. DD is the default input notation.

Add Conversion—Create a new output notation with a custom format.


The following functions are available in the output notation section:


Output Format Settings—Change the title of the output notation and supply a custom format for how to display coordinates.

Copy—Copy the coordinate to the clipboard.

Expand Output—Display coordinates as individual parts to allow copying each separately (such as only the Latitude coordinate for Lat/Lon).

Remove Coordinate—Remove a notation from the list of output notations.

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Track allows you to view and record your location and movement. The widget can retrieve your device's location and create individual points, or \"locations\", or record points continuously and create lines, or \"paths\". In addition to latitude and longitude, the widget records time, altitude, speed, orientation, and accuracy. Locations and paths become output data sources, meaning you can use data you create with the track widget with other widgets, such as the Table widget and List widget.

"},"id":"widget_2522"},"widget_2523":{"uri":"widgets/layout/row/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Block 567","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"number":[40,10,40,10],"unit":"px"}}},"id":"widget_2523","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1570"}}},"widget_2524":{"uri":"widgets/common/image/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Image 343","config":{"functionConfig":{"altText":"","toolTip":"","linkParam":{},"scale":"Fit","imageParam":{"url":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2524/1720436396295.png","originalUrl":"${appResourceUrl}/images/widget_2524/1720436396295.png","fileName":"1720436396295.png","originalName":"chrome_qfC4agEaOE.png","imgSourceType":"BY_UPLOAD","fileFormat":"image/png","originalId":"1720436396295","isUseCompress":false,"originalWidth":469,"originalHeight":546},"imgSourceType":"","srcExpression":null,"imageFillMode":"FIT"},"styleConfig":{}},"id":"widget_2524","style":{"borderRadius":null,"border":{"color":"var(--light-300)","type":"solid","width":"2px"}}},"widget_2525":{"uri":"widgets/layout/column/","version":"1.20.0","label":"Column 695","config":{"space":10,"style":{"padding":{"space":[10],"unit":"px"},"justifyContent":"flex-start","alignItems":"stretch"}},"id":"widget_2525","layouts":{"DEFAULT":{"LARGE":"layout_1571"}}},"widget_2526":{"uri":"widgets/common/text/","version":"1.21.0","label":"Text 621","config":{"placeholder":"

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

The track panel provides users with the following options:


Get location—Retrieve a new point. This button appears if Watch location is turned off in the widget settings.

Start watching—Start continuously retrieving locations. This button appears if Watch location is turned on in the widget settings.

End watching—Finish retrieving locations. This generates a path.

Trace a path—Manually create a path. You can do this while watching is running.

Show from the Map or Hide from the Map—Show or hide symbols for locations on the map.

You can delete individual records with the Delete the record button or delete all records with the Clear results button.

Double click to edit text

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Moving Around The Map - Zoom In

Using a mouse with a scroll wheel - Move your mouse cursor to anywhere on the map and scroll the mouse wheel forwards.

Using the Zoom In button (+) - Click the top left corner of the map. This zooms in on the current centre of the map.

Zoom to a rectangle -

  1. Move your cursor to the top left corner of the rectangle to be drawn.
  2. Hold the SHIFT key down on your keyboard, hold down the key on your mouse you would normally use to position the cursor (or on your laptop mousepad), then drag the cursor to the bottom right of the rectangle. A red rectangle appears on the screen.
  3. Release the mouse key and SHIFT key to zoom in to the area of the rectangle.

","style":{"verticalAlign":"center","wrap":true},"text":"

Moving Around The Map - Zoom Out

  1. Using a mouse with a scroll wheel - Move your mouse cursor to anywhere on the map and scroll the mouse wheel backwards. The map zooms out.
  2. Using the Zoom Out button (-) - Click the top left corner of the map. This zooms out from the current centre of the map.
